ca_temple_of_ishtar.blurb: Temple of Ishtar is the westernmost of the major formations at Texas Canyon, in the high desert hills north of Los Angeles. Seen from the east it looks like a gentle slab, but the southwest and west sides drop into steep, knobby walls carrying fifteen routes, nearly all bolted sport lines with a single trad route. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up to the low 5.12s, with most climbs between 5.8 and 5.11, so there is something for a mixed group. The conglomerate is pocketed and fluted, and it is brittle: holds can snap and the stone is easily damaged when damp, so a helmet is wise. Only a couple of minutes over the ridge from the neighbouring Chicken formation.

ca_warlock_the.blurb: The Warlock is a big, triple-stepped tower that caps the end of the ridge in the Needles, a cluster of spires above the Kern River in the southern Sierra, at roughly 7,500 feet. It is a trad-only venue with fifteen routes graded from 5.9 into the 5.12s, most of them in the 5.10 range. Lines wander from short, punchy cracks to long multi-pitch outings of up to around ten pitches, and there are climbs on every side of the tower. The main ridge trail leads to the upper faces on the north, west and east, while lower routes need a rappel or a longer detour. Expect a remote, quiet setting with a long walk in and two-rope rappels to get down.

ca_tahoe_donner_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder tucked into the trees just outside Donner Lake, in the Tahoe Donner neighbourhood near Truckee, at about 6,400 feet. It is the best developed block among the Bermgarten boulders, with fourteen recorded problems running from V0 up to V5; roughly half sit in the easy-to-moderate range and a handful reach V4 and V5. The base has been cleaned up, most lines have good landings, and there is a fair amount of tree shade, which makes it a handy spot to rack up mileage on a short outing. The walk from the car is only a few minutes on the rim trail, then a spur toward the power lines.
ca_tahoe_donner_boulder.parking_note: Leave the car in the unpaved lot where Bermgarten Road ends, inside the Tahoe Donner neighbourhood.

ca_hollow_the.blurb: The Hollow is the first cluster of boulders you meet on the walk upstream along Lewis Creek, in the Sierra foothills a short drive from Oakhurst, at about 3,900 feet. It is regarded as the most varied group at the creek, and all fourteen problems are bouldering. Plenty of the climbs are easy warm-ups on friendly landings, which suits beginners, while a scattering of sit-starts and harder problems reach into the V5 to V7 range. Expect a creekside setting where a rock-hop across the water is needed for some of the stones, with a lot of the grade spread sitting between V0 and V4.

ca_boy_named_sue_boulder_the.blurb: This is a compact, roughly fifteen-foot boulder among the Rock Creek boulders in the eastern Sierra, at around 8,500 feet in a shaded stand of mixed forest beside flowing streams. Fourteen problems are recorded, running from an easy V0 through the middle grades and on to a cluster of hard lines in the V7 to V11 range. The climbing rewards careful footwork and balance far more than raw power, and the stone is smooth with good friction, so combinations and eliminates are common. The walk in crosses two streams on fallen logs that get slick when wet. Bring at least two pads. Late spring through early fall is the comfortable window.
